formality: Formal register ("u/uw"), never "je/jij" — confirmed throughout the existing UI ("Weet u het zeker?", "Controleer uw invoer", "Uw sessie is verlopen. Log opnieuw in.").
styleNotes: 1) Keep established English loanwords for hashcat/infra-specific nouns exactly as the shipped app already does (hash, potfile, keyspace, chunk, workflow, benchmark, overflow, voucher, claimcode, cloud fleet, provisioning, webhook, dashboard, budget, SAN) rather than inventing Dutch equivalents — several drafted terms had drifted from the live app and are corrected here (wordlist→woordenlijst not woordlijst, attack mode→aanvalsmodus not aanvalstype, chunk→chunk not blok, workflow→workflow not werkstroom, claim code→claimcode not inschrijvingscode, cloud fleet→cloud fleet not cloudbatterij). 2) Noun-noun compounds are written as one word (hashlijst, woordenlijst, hashsnelheid, auditlogboek, wachtwoordhergebruik), except when the first element is itself a borrowed attack-mode name, which takes a hyphen before the Dutch suffix (Associatie-aanvalsmodus, Combinatie-aanvalsmodus, woordenboek-aanval) — confirmed by admin.json's '*-aanvalsmodus' strings. 3) 'Taak' (job) and 'subtaak' (task — one chunk assignment on one agent) are distinct levels of the same hierarchy in the shipped UI (Taken vs. Subtaken/Subtaak-ID) and must never be collapsed into the same word. 4) Capitalize only as the surrounding UI string requires (sentence case for labels); the glossary entries below give the dictionary/base form.

hash.note: Standard loanword throughout the UI (hashType, hashRate, plural 'Hashes' in hashlists.json/analytics.json) — never translated.

hashlist.note: Matches the established, extensively used term (Hashlijst/Hashlijsten, Hashlijstbeheer, Hashlijst-details) throughout hashlists.json and jobs.json.

hash type.note: One word; matches the dominant existing form (Hashtype) in jobs.json, hashlists.json and pot.json. One outlier, 'Hash-type', appears in analytics.json but is inconsistent with the rest of the app — don't propagate the hyphen.

crack.note: Infinitive verb; matches existing nominalized use ('Kraken voltooid op' in jobs.json). Note the same word 'Kraken' is also used in the app as the plural noun for recovered cracks (cracksFound columns) — a pre-existing overload, not something to fix here.

cracked.note: Past participle used as adjective/label; matches 'Gekraakt' column in hashlists.json.

cracked hashes.note: Exact match for the widely used phrase ('Gekraakte hashes' in dashboard.json, navigation.json, and throughout pot.json).

plaintext.note: Changed from kept-English. Every existing occurrence translates this literally as 'platte tekst' (admin.json apiKeySecurityNote, analytics.json hashReuseAnalysis and internalUseOnly) — the English word 'plaintext' does not appear anywhere in the app. Separately: when the UI shows the actual recovered value to a user it just says 'Wachtwoord' (Password), e.g. hashlists.json hashDetails — use 'platte tekst' only for the generic technical concept, not as a relabel of that field.

potfile.note: hashcat-specific filename convention; kept throughout (Potfile-instellingen, potfile-batchverwerking) — never translated.

client potfile.note: Changed from 'client-potfile'. 'Client' is always translated as 'klant' in this app (Klant, Klantbeheer, Klantnaam) — it would be inconsistent to keep it in English only in this one compound. 'Potfile' itself stays an English loanword, matching the Potfile-instellingen pattern of [English noun]-[Dutch noun]; here the order is reversed, so 'klant-potfile' keeps the hyphen for legibility.

wordlist.note: Changed from 'woordlijst'. The established, extremely frequent term everywhere in the app is 'woordenlijst/woordenlijsten' (Woordenlijstbeheer, Woordenlijst uploaden, Eerste/Tweede woordenlijst, hybride woordenlijst + masker). 'Woordlijst' does not appear anywhere in the shipped UI.

rule file.note: Confirmed directly: admin.json enableRuleSplittingHelper says 'Automatisch grote regelbestanden splitsen...' — plural 'regelbestanden' matches this singular exactly.

charset.note: No existing occurrence to confirm against (feature not yet surfaced in nl locale strings), but this is the standard Dutch IT rendering and is not contradicted anywhere.

attack mode.note: Changed from 'aanvalstype'. 'Aanvalsmodus' is the term used consistently and repeatedly (jobs.json 'Aanvalsmodus', admin.json 'Vereisten aanvalsmodus' plus every '...-aanvalsmodus' string). 'Aanvalstype' does not appear anywhere in the product.

brute force.note: Matches the mode label 'Brute-force' (jobs.json attackModes.bruteforce). Note the app's own compound with 'aanvalsmodus' is written with a space instead, 'Brute force-aanvalsmodus' (admin.json) — a minor pre-existing inconsistency, not something to imitate when 'brute force' stands alone.

dictionary attack.note: Hyphenated to match the established pattern of [mode-name noun]-aanval(smodus): 'Straight-aanvalsmodus', 'Combinatie-aanvalsmodus', 'Associatie-aanvalsmodus' (all admin.json). The bare mode-dropdown label itself is just 'Woordenboek' without 'aanval' — that's a different, shorter context (jobs.json attackModes.dictionary) and not a contradiction.

hybrid attack.note: Two words, no hyphen — matches 'Hybride aanvalsmodus' / 'hybride aanval met woordenlijst' (admin.json). Unlike the noun-name compounds above, 'hybride' is a plain adjective, which this app never hyphenates onto the following noun.

association attack.note: Matches the hyphenation convention confirmed by admin.json's 'Associatie-aanvalsmodus'.

keyspace.note: Matches the dominant usage (jobs.json common.keyspace, layerTable.keyspace; analytics.json 'Totaal geschatte keyspace'). One outlier exists — dashboard.json translates it as 'Sleutelruimte' — which is inconsistent with the rest of the app; standardize on 'keyspace' rather than imitating that outlier.

effective keyspace.note: Exact match for the existing 'Effectieve keyspace' column label (jobs.json layerTable and common sections).

chunk.note: Changed from 'blok'. The app keeps 'chunk' as an English loanword compounded directly onto Dutch nouns throughout: 'Chunkgrootte', 'Chunkduur', 'Taakchunking', 'Chunkfluctuatiepercentage', 'Regelchunk-map', 'Maximum regelchunks'. 'Blok' never appears for this concept.

task.note: Changed from 'taak'. A task (one chunk assignment on one agent) is consistently called 'subtaak' in this app — the Job Details 'Subtaken' tab, 'Subtaak-ID' columns, 'Opnieuw uitvoeren van subtaak mislukt' — specifically to distinguish it from the job-level 'taak'. Reusing 'taak' for both concepts (as the draft did) would collapse a real UI distinction.

job.note: Matches 'Taken' (page title), 'Taak aanmaken', 'Taakdetails' throughout jobs.json. See 'task' above for why this must stay distinct from 'subtaak'.

preset job.note: Changed from 'vooraf ingestelde taak'. The app uses the single compound adjective 'vooringesteld': 'vooringestelde taken toevoegen', 'Zoek naar vooringestelde taken' (admin.json workflows section).

workflow.note: Changed from 'werkstroom'. Kept fully in English everywhere: 'Workflow aanmaken', 'Workflowstappen', 'Workflownaam', 'Taakworkflows' (navigation.json, admin.json). 'Werkstroom' does not appear anywhere in the product.

loopback.note: Matches 'Loopback', 'Loopback inschakelen voor alle geschikte stappen' (admin.json).

max agents.note: Changed from 'max. agenten'. The established label is 'Max. agents' (dashboard.json, jobs.json, admin.json) — the plural stays the English 'agents', matching how 'agent' itself is pluralized in this app (see 'agent' below); Dutch 'agenten' does not appear.

hash rate.note: Changed from 'hash-snelheid'. Written as one word everywhere it appears: 'Hashsnelheid' (agents.json ×2, dashboard.json), 'Gecombineerde hashsnelheid' (jobs.json) — never hyphenated.

agent.note: Singular is identical in English and Dutch. Plural is kept English, 'agents' (agents.json title, 'Actieve agents' in admin.json) rather than Dutch 'agenten' — confirms the fix to 'max agents' above.

claim code.note: Changed from 'inschrijvingscode', which does not appear anywhere in the product. The established, UI-wide term is 'claimcode' (one word): 'Claimcode', 'Uw claimcode:', 'Genereren van claimcode mislukt' (agents.json).

voucher.note: Matches 'Voucher', 'Vouchers', 'Vouchercode' throughout agents.json. Distinct, established term from 'claimcode' even though terms.json treats them as synonyms — the UI uses both words for slightly different contexts (voucher = the registration record; claimcode = the code string itself) and both should be kept as-is.

heartbeat.note: No existing nl-locale occurrence either way. Kept English as a reasonable default alongside the app's other kept networking/infra terms (webhook, API, TLS, SSL).

offline buffer.note: Changed from hyphenated 'offline-buffer'. The one existing string keeps this as two plain English words: 'Agent Offline Buffer' (notifications.json title) — not hyphenated.

auto-update.note: No exact existing phrase to confirm against (the one related string, admin.json applyNote, phrases it descriptively as '...ontvangen updates automatisch'), but this matches the app's established 'automatisch(e) + noun' pattern used elsewhere ('Automatische aggregatie', 'automatisch aanmaken').

binary.note: Changed from 'binair bestand'. When referring to the managed hashcat executable itself, the app keeps the English noun unchanged and even uses the English plural: 'Hashcat binary' (agents.json hashcatBinary), 'Geen agent-binaries beschikbaar' (agents.json noAgentBinaries). Reserve the translated adjective 'binair' for unrelated generic file-type descriptions, e.g. hashlists.json's 'uitvoerbaar binair bestand' for a generic uploaded executable — that is a different concept, not this feature.

client.note: Matches 'Klant', 'Klantbeheer', 'Klantnaam' throughout hashlists.json, admin.json, navigation.json. See 'client potfile' above — this translation must be applied consistently in compounds too.

team.note: No existing nl-locale occurrence (the multi-team feature is still planned, not yet built/localized). 'Team' is a widely adopted loanword in Dutch and a reasonable default; revisit once the feature ships and real strings exist.

member.note: No existing occurrence (same unshipped feature as 'team'). Standard Dutch term; plural 'leden'.

archive.note: Changed from the noun 'archief'. The term describes an action ('hide from default lists without deleting'), and the app's established rendering is the verb 'Archiveren' with adjective/status 'Gearchiveerd' for the resulting state (jobs.json, hashlists.json archive sections) — not the noun 'archief', which describes a storage place, a different concept.

analytics report.note: Matches the plural 'analyserapporten' used in analytics.json's page description.

hash reuse.note: Matches 'Geen hash-hergebruik gedetecteerd' (analytics.json noHashReuse) exactly. Note the app also has a longer descriptive rendering, 'Hash-gebaseerd wachtwoordhergebruik', used as a report section title (analytics.json hashReuse) — that's a section heading, not the base-term translation; use the shorter compound as the glossary term.

settings.note: Confirmed via consistent compounds throughout the app: 'Klantinstellingen', 'Meldingsinstellingen', 'Planningsinstellingen'.

autosave.note: No existing occurrence found, but matches the app's established 'automatisch + verb' pattern (see 'auto-update').

apply.note: Confirmed by admin.json: 'na het toepassen van wijzigingen' ('after applying changes').

SAN.note: No existing nl-locale occurrence (the certificate-SAN admin feature is not yet localized), but this is the correct call — it's a fixed technical abbreviation (Subject Alternative Name) that Dutch security professionals use as-is.

network share.note: No existing occurrence (feature in progress, not yet localized). 'Netwerkshare' is the natural Dutch IT rendering, keeping 'share' as an understood English loanword — reasonable default to apply once the feature ships.

mount.note: No direct existing occurrence for network-share mounting specifically, but matches the app's established verb for 'attach/link' elsewhere: settings.json 'Account koppelen' (link account) / 'Ontkoppelen' (unlink).

cloud fleet.note: Changed from 'cloudbatterij', which does not appear anywhere. 'Cloud Fleet' is kept fully in English as the section title in both navigation.json and admin.json.

provisioning.note: Changed from 'inrichting'. Kept as an English loanword throughout: the section title is literally 'Cloud Provisioning' (navigation.json, admin.json), and it's also compounded directly onto a Dutch noun elsewhere, 'Gebruikersprovisioning' (admin.json) — 'inrichting' does not appear.

budget.note: Matches 'Cloudbudget' (jobs.json cloud_budget_blocked) and compounds consistently as an English loanword.

threshold.note: Matches the one existing precedent, 'Regelsplitsingsdrempel' (admin.json). Newer cloud-budget threshold strings in admin.json are still shipped as untranslated English placeholders ('Threshold policy', etc.) — that's translation debt in that in-progress feature, not evidence against 'drempel' as the right term.

drain.note: Changed from 'uitputten'. The one existing string keeps this fully in English, 'Draining' (admin.json), rather than translating it. Dutch sysadmins/DevOps commonly loan this verb directly ('een instance draineren') the same way as 'updaten' or 'downloaden'; 'uitputten' literally means 'to exhaust/deplete' and doesn't clearly convey 'stop accepting new work, let what's running finish'.

teardown.note: No existing nl-locale occurrence (shipped as untranslated English placeholders, e.g. admin.json 'Teardown is failing'). 'Afbraak' is a natural, understandable Dutch noun for destroying a cloud instance; kept as a reasonable default.

backup codes.note: Changed from hyphenated 'back-upcodes'. Established as one word throughout: 'Backupcode' (singular, auth.json), 'Backupcodes' (settings.json), 'Aantal backupcodes' (admin.json).

session.note: Matches 'Sessie', 'Sessie beëindigen' throughout common.json, errors.json, admin.json.

API key.note: Exact match throughout admin.json ('API-sleutel', 'API-sleutelbeheer', 'Intrekken van API-sleutel').
